title: A group of jinn listened and were amazed.
subtitle: Unseen listeners at a dawn prayer
then: The introduction relates from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet ﷺ led Fajr at Nakhlah while travelling with Companions. {idea}A company of jinn passed, stopped, and listened attentively.{/idea} Allah told him ﷺ to inform his people that {idea}the jinn believed and affirmed it.{/idea}
now: You have heard the same surahs in every Taraweeh since you were a child. They play in the background while you cook. {idea}Some listeners hear it once and are stunned.{/idea} When did you last let it amaze you?
old: I know the Quran already. It is familiar background.
new: The Quran is wondrous. Familiarity is the only thing dulling it.
try: Listen to one short surah today as if hearing it for the first time.

title: It guides to what is right, so we believed.
subtitle: Hearing, recognising, committing
then: The jinn did not debate. Ibn Kathir says right course means {idea}what is correct and leads to success.{/idea} They heard, saw the guidance in it, believed, and promised {idea}we will never associate anyone with our Lord.{/idea}
now: You hear a reminder that hits you at a friend's wedding, a funeral, a random clip online. You think: that is true. Then you scroll on. {idea}The jinn heard and acted in the same breath.{/idea}
old: Agreeing with a reminder is enough.
new: When guidance rings true, the right reply is a commitment.
try: Take one line of Quran that moved you recently and act on it today.

title: Our Lord is too exalted for a wife or son.
subtitle: The jinn's first lesson about Allah
then: Ibn Abbas said Jadd means {idea}His actions, commands and power{/idea}, and also His blessings on creation. Mujahid said it is His magnificence. When the jinn believed, {idea}they declared Him far above taking a spouse or a child.{/idea}
now: It is natural to imagine Allah the way we imagine a powerful person: moods, needs, family. {idea}The jinn's first realisation was that He is nothing like that.{/idea} He needs nothing. Everything needs Him.
old: I picture Allah somewhat like a very powerful person.
new: Allah is exalted beyond anything I can compare Him to.
try: Read Surah Al-Ikhlas slowly today and reflect on each line.

title: Our fool used to say outrageous things about Allah.
subtitle: Realising who had been misleading them
then: Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and As-Suddi said the foolish one meant {trap}Iblis.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds it includes anyone who claims Allah has a spouse or son. Hearing the Quran, the jinn saw their old leader for {trap}what he was.{/trap}
now: There is always a voice that sounds sure of itself: a podcast host, a loud uncle, an influencer with a theory about God. {idea}Confidence is not the same as truth.{/idea}
old: If someone speaks confidently about religion, they probably know.
new: Anyone who says things about Allah without knowledge is foolish, however sure they sound.
try: Before sharing anything about Allah today, check its source first.

title: We never imagined anyone would lie about Allah.
subtitle: How trust kept them misled
then: Ibn Kathir explains their words: {trap}we did not think humans and jinn would join together in lying about Allah.{/trap} So they believed it. {idea}When they heard the Quran, they knew it had been a lie.{/idea}
now: A forwarded message in the family group: a hadith with no source, a story about a miracle. You assume no one would make that up about religion. {trap}People do.{/trap}
old: Nobody would invent things about religion, so what I hear must be true.
new: Even religious claims need checking. The Quran is the measure.
try: Next time a religious forward arrives, verify it before believing or sharing.

title: Seeking refuge in jinn only made the fear grow.
subtitle: Turning to the wrong protector
then: Ibn Kathir says pre-Islamic Arabs entering a valley would say: {trap}I seek refuge with the master of this valley.{/trap} Seeing their fear, the jinn {trap}increased them in fear and terror{/trap} and grew bolder against them. Ikrimah said the jinn had feared humans until then.
now: The lucky charm in the car. The horoscope you check before a big day. The fortune teller your aunt swears by. {trap}Every false shelter feeds the fear it promised to calm.{/trap} Seeking refuge belongs to Allah alone.
old: A little superstition is harmless and makes me feel safer.
new: Turning to anything but Allah for protection only grows the fear.
try: When you feel uneasy somewhere today, say a'udhu billah and mean it.

title: They thought, as you did, that no messenger would come.
subtitle: Giving up on guidance arriving
then: Al-Kalbi and Ibn Jarir said they thought {trap}Allah would never send a messenger after such a long time.{/trap} The jinn were telling their people they had shared the same mistake as the humans of Makkah.
now: You have been asking for guidance on a decision for months and feel nothing. Or you feel far from Allah and think it is too late for anything to change. {reward}Guidance came after centuries of silence. It can reach you too.{/reward}
old: It has been so long, guidance will not come to me now.
new: Allah sends guidance after long silences. It is never too late.
try: Make istikhara or a sincere dua for guidance on one decision today.

title: We reached for the sky and found it guarded.
subtitle: The heavens sealed when revelation came
then: Ibn Kathir says when the Quran was revealed, Allah {reward}filled the sky with stern guards{/reward} so devils could not steal from it and pass it to soothsayers. He did this {reward}out of kindness and mercy to His servants{/reward}, protecting His Book.
now: The Quran you scroll past on your phone was protected at the level of the sky. {idea}Allah guarded it so carefully because it matters that much.{/idea} The least we can do is open it.
old: The Quran is just one book among many.
new: Allah guarded the heavens to keep this message pure. It is that precious.
try: Open a mushaf today and read one page, slowly.

title: We used to eavesdrop. Now a flame waits.
subtitle: The old shortcut to hidden knowledge was closed
then: The jinn used to sit in places near the sky to steal a hearing. Ibn Kathir says now {trap}whoever tries finds a flame waiting in ambush{/trap}. Soothsayers had mixed stolen scraps with lies, so that {trap}no one knew who was truthful.{/trap}
now: The app that predicts your week. The psychic hotline ad. The friend who reads coffee cups. {idea}The door to hidden knowledge was closed when the Quran came.{/idea} What is left is guesswork.
old: Some people really can see what is coming.
new: The unseen belongs to Allah. Every shortcut to it was shut.
try: If you use any app or habit that predicts your future, delete or drop it today.

title: Is harm meant for earth, or guidance?
subtitle: Good manners even when speaking of the unknown
then: Ibn Kathir notes the jinn's {idea}good manners in phrasing{/idea}: they did not attribute evil to anyone, but {reward}attributed the good to Allah.{/reward} He cites the Prophet's ﷺ words: {idea}and evil is not attributed to You.{/idea}
now: Something hard happens and the first words out are "why is God doing this to me?" The jinn, facing something frightening, still chose their words carefully. {idea}How you speak about Allah in hard moments matters.{/idea}
old: When bad things happen, it is fair to say Allah did this to me.
new: Good is named to Allah. In hardship, I speak about Him with respect.
try: Next time something goes wrong today, say alhamdulillah ala kulli hal before anything else.

title: Some of us are righteous, some not. Many paths.
subtitle: Honesty about their own community
then: The jinn admit their own kind is divided. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said it means {idea}among us are believers and among us are disbelievers.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they were on many differing paths, with different thoughts and opinions.
now: Your family, your mosque, your friend group: it is easy to assume being part of it makes you fine. {idea}Every community has people on different paths.{/idea} The question is which path you are on.
old: Being part of a good community means I am on the right path.
new: Every group has many paths in it. I have to choose mine.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: which path am I on, not which group.

title: We cannot escape Allah, not on earth, not by running.
subtitle: Recognising there is nowhere to hide
then: Ibn Kathir explains their words: {idea}we know Allah's power is decisive over us{/idea}, and even if we try to flee, He has complete control. This certainty was part of what moved them to believe.
now: You change cities, jobs, friend groups, phone numbers. The guilt comes with you. {idea}You cannot outrun Allah, but you can run to Him.{/idea} That is the only direction that works.
old: If I keep busy enough, I can avoid facing Allah.
new: There is no running from Allah, only running to Him.
try: Stop for two minutes today, sit still, and turn to Allah about one thing you avoid.

title: We heard the guidance and believed. No loss to fear.
subtitle: The security of the believer

key.label: What the believer need not fear

then: Ibn Kathir says the jinn were proud of believing, and {reward}it was something worth being proud of.{/reward} Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said the believer need not fear {reward}that his good deeds will be reduced, or that he will carry more than his own sins.{/reward}
now: You give in secret and wonder if it counted. You pray when tired and wonder if it was enough. {reward}Allah does not shrink your reward or add to your load.{/reward} Nothing you do for Him is lost.
old: My small good deeds probably do not count for much.
new: Nothing good I do is lost, and I carry nothing that is not mine.
try: Do one small good deed today and trust it is fully counted.

title: Those who submit have sought out the right way.
subtitle: The just and the unjust among them
then: Ibn Kathir says the Qasit is {trap}one who behaves unjustly with the truth and deviates from it{/trap}, the opposite of the one who is just. Those who submit {reward}sought salvation for themselves.{/reward}
now: Choosing to pray on a work trip, to turn down the deal that is a bit dishonest. It can feel like giving something up. {reward}The verse calls it searching for the right way{/reward}, and finding it.
old: Submitting to Allah means losing things I want.
new: Submitting is how I find the right way and save myself.
try: Make one choice today purely because it is what Allah wants.

title: The unjust become fuel for the Fire.
subtitle: Those who swerve from the truth
then: The jinn finish their contrast. Ibn Kathir says the Qasit is {trap}one who behaves unjustly with the truth and turns from it.{/trap} Such people become {trap}fuel used to kindle the Fire.{/trap} The words are sober, a warning to their own people.
now: You know what is right in that argument with your sibling, but you defend your side anyway. You know the deal is unfair, but it benefits you. {idea}Injustice starts with refusing a truth you already see.{/idea}
old: Injustice is something big that criminals do.
new: Injustice begins when I turn away from a truth I can see.
try: Admit you were wrong about one thing today, to the person involved.

title: Stay straight on the path, and abundant water follows.
subtitle: Steadiness and provision
then: Ibn Kathir gives two views. Most, including Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, said if they {idea}stood firm on Islam{/idea} they would be given {reward}abundant provision.{/reward} Muqatil said it was revealed about Quraysh when {trap}deprived of rain for seven years.{/trap} Another view says plenty can also be a respite for the misguided.
now: Business is booming, the bonus came, the house is full. It feels like a sign. Or it is a lean year and you wonder what you did. {idea}Steadiness brings blessing, but plenty alone proves nothing.{/idea}
old: If I am doing well financially, Allah must be pleased with me.
new: Staying straight invites blessing. But abundance is never proof by itself.
try: Pick one good practice and keep it every day this week, rain or shine.

title: Plenty is a test. Turning away is the danger.
subtitle: What abundance is for
then: Zayd bin Aslam said the test is {idea}to see who will remain on guidance and who will turn back to sin.{/idea} Whoever turns from the remembrance of his Lord faces a punishment Ibn Abbas called {trap}harsh, with no relief in it.{/trap}
now: The promotion means longer hours. The new car means weekend drives instead of Jumu'ah. Good things arrive, and quietly push out remembrance. {idea}The test is not the blessing. It is whether you forget Him in it.{/idea}
old: When life is good, I do not need to worry about my faith.
new: Good times are a test too. The danger is forgetting Allah in them.
try: When something good happens today, stop and say alhamdulillah before you enjoy it.

title: The places of prayer belong to Allah alone.
subtitle: Call on no one alongside Him
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah commands His servants to {idea}single Him out alone for worship.{/idea} Sa'id bin Jubayr reported that the jinn asked how they could attend the masjid and prayer while so far away, and this verse came: {idea}the masjids are for Allah.{/idea}
now: You walk into the masjid with your phone buzzing, a deal on your mind, someone you want to impress in the row behind. {idea}This place, and this moment, belong to Allah only.{/idea}
old: Prayer is mostly about showing up and going through it.
new: The place and the moment of prayer are for Allah alone, with no one beside Him.
try: Before your next prayer, put your phone away and say: this is for You alone.

title: When he stood to pray, they crowded around him.
subtitle: A crowd that pressed in
then: Ibn Kathir lists three views. The jinn pressed close {idea}from eagerness to hear.{/idea} Or they were amazed at how the Companions moved as one in prayer. Or, the view Ibn Jarir preferred, {trap}humans and jinn crowded together to put out the message{/trap}, but {reward}Allah supported it and made it prevail.{/reward}
now: You stand up for prayer at a work party, and every eye turns to you. Some curious, some annoyed. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ stood up for Allah with a crowd pressing against him, and the message won.{/reward}
old: Standing out for my faith will just bring pressure.
new: Standing up for Allah may draw a crowd. He supports what is His.
try: Pray on time today even if people around you will notice.

title: Say: I call only on my Lord.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ reply to the pressure
then: Ibn Kathir says when they {trap}harmed him, opposed him and united against him{/trap}, the Prophet ﷺ answered: {idea}I only worship my Lord alone. I seek His help and put my trust in Him.{/idea}
now: The meeting where everyone is against your idea. The family that disagrees with your choice. You could fight every one of them. {idea}Or you could turn first to the One who controls hearts.{/idea}
old: When everyone is against me, I have to fight my own corner.
new: Under pressure, my first move is to call on my Lord and trust Him.
try: Before your next hard conversation, make a short dua asking Allah for help.

title: I have no power to harm you or guide you.
subtitle: Even the Prophet ﷺ does not control hearts
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}I am only a man like you who receives revelation{/idea}, a servant of Allah. {idea}I have no control over your guidance or misguidance{/idea}; all of it belongs to Allah.
now: You have tried everything to get your son to pray. You feel like a failure every Friday he stays in bed. {idea}If the Prophet ﷺ could not force guidance, neither can you.{/idea} Your part is to convey, love, and make dua.
old: If someone I love is not religious, I have failed them.
new: Guidance is in Allah's hands. My part is to convey kindly and pray.
try: Make dua for the person you most want guided, then let the weight go.

title: No one could shelter me from Allah.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ names his own need
then: Even the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}if I disobeyed Allah, no one could rescue me.{/idea} Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi said refuge means {idea}a place to escape to{/idea}, and there is none besides Him.
now: You assume the imam, the scholar, the pious aunt are fine; they do not need to worry. The best of creation said he had no refuge except Allah. {idea}Everyone runs to the same place.{/idea}
old: Really righteous people do not need to worry about Allah's punishment.
new: Even the best of creation sought refuge only in Allah. So do I.
try: Say a'udhu billah today with full attention, once, as a real request.

title: My task is only to deliver His message.
subtitle: Conveying is what saves the messenger
then: Ibn Kathir says the meaning is: {idea}nothing saves me except conveying the Message I was given.{/idea} He links it to the command: {idea}O Messenger, proclaim what was sent to you.{/idea} After that, whoever disobeys {trap}faces the Fire, with no escape.{/trap}
now: You have heard the message: in khutbahs, in your parents' home, on your own screen. {idea}It has been delivered to you.{/idea} What happens next is your part.
old: It is up to religious people to convince me.
new: The message has reached me. Now the choice is mine.
try: Pass on one good piece of knowledge to someone today, simply and kindly.

title: Then they will know who was weaker and fewer.
subtitle: Numbers look different on the Day
then: The opponents of the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah outnumbered the believers. Ibn Kathir says on the Day they will see {trap}who has the weaker helpers and fewer numbers{/trap}: the idolaters have {trap}no helper at all{/trap}, and are fewer than the soldiers of Allah.
now: You are the only one at work who fasts. The only one in your class who does not drink. It feels like you are the odd one out. {reward}On the Day, being with Allah is the majority.{/reward}
old: If most people around me live differently, maybe I am wrong.
new: Numbers today mean nothing. Allah's side is the stronger one.
try: Reach out to one other person who shares your faith at work or school today.

title: I do not know if it is near or far.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ did not know the Hour
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ had {idea}no knowledge of when the Hour would be.{/idea} When a man asked when, he ﷺ replied: {idea}what have you prepared for it?{/idea} The man said: only love for Allah and His Messenger. He ﷺ said: {reward}you will be with whom you love.{/reward}
now: Videos claiming the end-times date. Threads counting the signs. It is easy to get pulled into guessing. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ turned the question around: what have you prepared?{/idea}
old: Knowing when the end comes would help me get ready.
new: The date is Allah's. My job is the preparing, and the loving.
try: Ask yourself the Prophet's ﷺ question today: what have I prepared? Write one answer.

title: He alone knows the unseen and reveals it to no one.
subtitle: The limits of all created knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the verse that {idea}they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills.{/idea} No one in creation can reach any of His knowledge except what Allah allows. The jinn in this surah had once tried to steal it.
now: The doctor gives a prognosis. The economist predicts a crash. Your own anxiety writes the ending in advance. {idea}None of them hold the unseen.{/idea} Only Allah does, and He is kind.
old: I can figure out what is going to happen if I think hard enough.
new: The unseen is Allah's. I can plan, then leave the outcome with Him.
try: When you catch yourself predicting the worst today, say: Allah knows, I do not.

title: Except a messenger He chooses, guarded front and back.
subtitle: How revelation was protected on its way
then: Ibn Kathir says this includes both the angelic and human messenger. Allah gives him {reward}extra guardian angels{/reward} who protect him and accompany the revelation. Sa'id bin Jubayr said {reward}four guardian angels along with Jibril.{/reward}
now: A parcel worth millions travels with a security escort. The Quran in your bag travelled with angels around it. {idea}What was guarded that carefully deserves to be opened.{/idea}
old: Who knows how much of the message reached us accurately.
new: Allah guarded revelation with angels so it reached us whole.
try: Read the Quran today with the thought that angels guarded these words to reach you.

title: He surrounds all they hold and counts everything.
subtitle: Nothing escapes His counting
then: Qatadah said it means the Prophet ﷺ would know {idea}the messengers had conveyed and the angels had protected them.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that Allah {idea}knows all things before they occur{/idea}, and so the surah closes: He encompasses all and {reward}keeps count of everything.{/reward}
now: The tired prayer at midnight. The coin dropped in a charity box. The angry text you did not send. {reward}Every one is counted.{/reward} Nothing you do for Him is too small to be numbered.
old: Most of my small efforts get lost and do not matter.
new: Allah counts every single thing. No sincere effort goes unrecorded.
try: Do three small good deeds today and trust each one is counted.
